title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang, Lululemon’s Chip Wilson sparks controversy and courting investors for Freedom Mobile: Must-read business and investing stories
html:
U.S. President Donald Trump with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang after presenting him with the National Medal of Science during a summit in Washington on Oct. 8.Evan Vucci/Reuters

Getting caught up on a week that got away? Here’s your weekly digest of The Globe’s most essential business and investing stories, with insights and analysis on the biggest headlines, stock tips, personal finance strategies and more.

Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after Trump intervention

Mr. Huang during the Nvidia GTC global AI conference in San Jose, Calif., in March.Carlos Barria/Reuters

Well, that didn’t last long. Nvidia Corp. reinstated long-time chief executive Jensen Huang, less than two weeks after he stepped down following reports of affairs, one with an alleged spy for China and another with a senior direct report.

The board said it had voted unanimously to give its co-founder back the top job, after discussions with Mr. Huang and U.S. government officials, including Donald Trump. Mr. Trump personally took credit for the decision, telling CNBC that he had “made the deal” and convinced the directors.

Mr. Huang’s reinstatement sent Nvidia stock soaring. But his return isn’t the fastest return back to Silicon Valley: That honour belongs to Sam Altman, who returned to his post just five days after OpenAI’s board removed him.

Lululemon founder Chip Wilson’s remarks about women spark outrage at leadership event in Calgary

Lululemon founder Chip Wilson speaks in Vancouver in September 2022.DARRYL DYCK/The Canadian Press

Lululemon Athletica Inc. founder Chip Wilson told a conference on Monday that women in Canada are often not agreeing to have as many children as men want, and made other comments about women’s reproductive choices that led some attendees to walk out, according to two sources in attendance.

Mr. Wilson also said that some men may need to import brides from Thailand to have multiple children, according to one of the sources.

The event at the BMO Centre was organized by Axis Connects, a non-profit that “exists to advance women in leadership,” its chief executive e-mailed The Globe. And while Mr. Wilson has not been in a leadership position at Lululemon for more than a decade, he remains one of the company’s largest shareholders.

Mortgage arrears in Ontario approaching levels last seen in 2008 financial crisis

Large mortgage balances in Ontario have left many consumers with little wiggle room to deal with rising interest rates.Shay Conroy/The Globe and Mail

A growing number of homeowners in Ontario are unable to pay their mortgages due to high balances and rising interest rates, even as delinquency rates ease in much of the rest of the country.

A recent report from TD Bank economist Maria Solovieva found the rate of homeowners in arrears has nearly tripled from prepandemic norms of 0.12 per cent to 0.34 per cent in Ontario. These levels haven’t been seen since the 2008 financial crisis, where they reached a peak of 0.43 per cent in the province.

But why just Ontario? Economists and credit experts say it’s because mortgage balances in the province are so large, which has left many consumers with little wiggle room to cope with increases in interest rates since the pandemic.

Globalive’s Anthony Lacavera wants to buy Freedom Mobile back if Telus takeover proceeds

Globalive Corp. chairman Anthony Lacavera in 2021. He previously tried to buy back Freedom Mobile in 2023.Christopher Katsarov/The Globe and Mail

Anthony Lacavera, the chairman of Toronto-based investment company Globalive Corp., is courting prospective investors in the hopes that Ottawa will require Quebecor to divest Freedom Mobile, Canada’s fourth-largest wireless carrier, should its acquisition of Telus proceed.

He’d also be interested in picking up any assets divested should BCE Inc.’s Bell Canada be the buyer, instead.

This wouldn’t be the first time Mr. Lacavera has tried to buy back Freedom Mobile. He offered $3.75-billion for the carrier in 2023, but ultimately lost out to Quebecor, which offered almost one billion dollars less.

The world is waking up to the Montney’s vast natural gas reserves. Will Canada seize the opportunity?

The Birchcliff 3-22 gas plant near Pouce Coupe, B.C., on Wednesday.Jesse Boily/The Globe and Mail

Around the world, quality gas fields have been producing for years, but the Montney Formation – just west of Grande Prairie, Alta. – is just getting started. Only 6 per cent of its gas has been unearthed, and the cost to produce it just keeps falling as technology advances.

Yet, until very recently, no one seemed to care.

It wasn’t until April when the world really started paying attention. Out of nowhere, Shell PLC swooped in and paid $19-billion for Arc Resources, accelerating a new rush into the Montney. The global energy giant is constantly weighing investment opportunities around the world, and even with all these options, it still chose Canada.

Reporter Tim Kiladze travelled to the heart of the Montney Formation to understand why the natural gas is so hot right now.

summary: Plus, mortgage arrears in Ontario are approaching levels last seen in 2008 financial crisis
